senses.gloss:
श्नु A technical term used by Pāṇini for नु, the sign of the
 5th class of roots.

स्नु €2 P. (स्नौति, स्नुत)
—1 To drip, trickle, fall in drops, distil, drop, ooze or run out, leak out,
—2 To flow, stream.

स्नु m., n.
—1 Table-land.
—2 Top, surface (in general). (This word has no forms for the first five
 inflections and is optionally substituted for सानु after acc. dual).
स्नु f. A sinew, tendon, muscle.

स्नुत a. Oozed, dropped, flowed &c.; त्रिष्टुम्मांसात् स्नुतोऽनुष्टुब्जगत्यस्थ्नः
 प्रजापतेः Bhāg. 3. 12. 45.

स्नुषा A daughter-in-law; समुपास्यत पुत्रभोग्यया स्नुषयेवाविकृतेन्द्रियः
 श्रिया R. 8. 14, 15. 72.

स्नुस् €4 P. (स्नुस्यति)
—1 To disappear, become invisible.
—2 To take, accept.
स्नुह् €4 P. (स्नुह्यति, स्नुग्ध or स्नूढ) To vomit.

स्नुह्^1, स्नुहा, -हिः f., -ही
 The milk-hedge plant. [Raghunandana, the author of Kṛtyatattva
 (Jīvānandaʼs ed. of Smṛtitattva vol. II, 1895) quotes a verse from
 the Devīpurāṇa in connection with the worship of the goddess Manasā
 to get rid of the fear of snake-bite (cf. Dr. Kaneʼs History of Dharma-śāstra, vol. V. p. 125).
 He explains स्नुही as सिजुवृक्षः. The botanic
 name of the tree is Euphorbia Nerifolia (Mar. निवहुंग). It is a plant
 from the stem of which a sticky substance oozes out.]
[1] Correction submitted by on 20170124. note: missing virAma. Cf. other dictionaries.
